Dist-Koraput
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner in is jail custody since 25.04.2025 having been implicated under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n)/376(3)/498- A/323/506 read with Section 34 of IPC and 4(2)/6 of the POCSO Act and Section 4 of the D.P Act on the allegation alleged him (petitioner) that, he (petitioner) had committed rape on the victim- informant in the year 2019, while the informant was aged about 14 years and since then, he (petitioner) continued his sexual relationship with her.
3. I have already heard from the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Additional Standing Counsel for the state & the learned counsel for the informant/victim.

4. During the course of hearing of the bail application, the learned counsel for the informant/victim submitted that, the present age of the victim/informant is 22 years and she is staying unitedly with the petitioner as his wife and the victim has been blessed with a female child.

5. The learned ASC vehemently opposed the bail application of the Petitioner contending that, on the 1st day of commission of rape by the Petitioner on the informant in the year 2019, she (informant) was aged about 14 years and even though, the present age of the informant is 22 years,
still then, the offence of rape committed by the Petitioner against the minor informant cannot be wiped out, for which, he (petitioner) should not be allowed to go on bail.

6. When, presently the petitioner and the victim being two adults, they are leading their conjugal life happily as husband and wife and when, they have been blessed with a female child and when, the victim is not at all interested to keep the petitioner inside the bar, then at this juncture, by applying the principles of law enunciated by the Apex Court in a case between Biswajyoti Chatterjee Vrs. State of West Bengal and another reported in 2025 INSC 458, I find no justification to disallow the prayer for bail of the Petitioner.

entities.text: Biswajyoti Chatterjee Vrs. State of West Bengal and another reported in 2025 INSC 458
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Hence, the bail application filed by the petitioner is allowed 8.

He (petitioner) is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter with a condition that :-
(i) he (petitioner) shall not subject the victim/informant to torture in any manner in future.
9. Accordingly, the bail application filed by the petitioner is disposed of finally.
10. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted to the petitioner on proper application.
( ANANDA CHANDRA BEHERA) Vacation Judge Binayak Location: High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Ghenu Hantal vs State Of Odisha .....
